chunks: Yūnus, from Abū Ayyūb, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:
"He is not considered muḥṣan unless he has a woman with him upon whom he can close his door."

key_terms.امْرَأَةٌ: a woman, here referring to a wife in the legal context
key_terms.بَابَهُ: his door, signifying seclusion and marital privacy
key_terms.عِنْدَهُ: in his possession or presence, indicating availability
key_terms.مُحْصَنًا: legally protected through marriage; one who meets the condition of iḥṣān

ai.seo_question: What makes a person legally considered muḥṣan in the rulings of zina?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal criterion for being considered muḥṣan in the context of the rulings of zina. It indicates that iḥṣān depends on the existence of a marital situation in which a man has access to his wife in privacy.
